data.content_ref: inline:SRC_04 defines cross-cutting explanations as requiring transfer of explanatory primitives across lineage boundaries and makes its cross-lineage reference ratio C the key count, but its own first countercondition concedes that structural analogies may not require explicit primitive references. Since cross-cutting explanations frequently are structural analogies (as SRC_001 itself notes), C can be zero even when cross-cutting explanations are abundant, so the proposed count does not validly measure suppression of the phenomenon the problem is about.
